description.en: Set of concepts and categories, applicable to Risk Management as specified in ISO 31073:2022, that shows their properties and the relations between them

definition.value: statement of the overall intentions and direction of an organization (3.3.7) related to risk management (3.2.1)
form of communication intended to inform particular internal or external interested party (3.3.2) by providing information regarding the current state of risk (3.1.1) and its management
extent to which an organization (3.3.7) and/or interested party (3.3.2) is subject to an event (3.3.11)
process to modify risk (3.1.1)

scopeNote.value: Risk treatment can create new risks or modify existing risks.
Risk treatments that deal with negative consequences are sometimes referred to as “risk mitigation”, “risk elimination”, “risk prevention” and “risk reduction”.

note.value: modified — “and/or its magnitude” has been deleted from the definition

definition.value: process of comparing the results of risk analysis (3.3.15) with risk criteria (3.3.6) to determine whether the risk (3.1.1) is acceptable or tolerable

scopeNote.value: Risk evaluation assists in the decision about risk treatment (3.3.32).

definition.value: combination of circumstances expected to be favourable to objectives (3.1.2)

scopeNote.value: An opportunity to one party may pose a threat (3.3.13) to another.
An opportunity is a positive situation in which gain is likely and over which one has a fair level of control.
Taking or not taking an opportunity are both sources of risk (3.1.1).

note.value: modified — “risk control” has replaced “control” in Note 1 to entry

definition.value: continual checking, supervising, critically observing or determining the status in order to identify change from the performance level required or expected

scopeNote.value: Monitoring can be applied to a risk management framework, risk management process (3.3.1), risk (3.1.1) or risk control (3.3.33).

definition.value: measure that maintains and/or modifies risk (3.1.1)

scopeNote.value: Risk controls do not always exert the intended or assumed modifying effect.
Risk controls include, but are not limited to, any process, policy, device, practice, or other conditions and/or actions which maintain and/or modify risk.

definition.value: acceptance of the potential benefit of gain, or burden of loss, from a particular risk (3.1.1)

scopeNote.value: The level of risk (3.3.22) retained can depend on risk criteria (3.3.6).
Risk retention includes the acceptance of residual risks (3.3.38).

definition.value: chance of something happening

scopeNote.value: In risk management terminology, the word “likelihood” is used to refer to the chance of something happening, whether defined, measured or determined objectively or subjectively, qualitatively or quantitatively, and described using general terms or mathematically [such as a probability (3.3.19) or a frequency (3.3.20)].

The English term “likelihood” does not have a direct equivalent in some languages; instead, the equivalent of the term “probability” is often used. However, in English, “probability” is often narrowly interpreted as a mathematical term. Therefore, in risk management terminology, “likelihood” is used with the intent that it should have the same broad interpretation as the term “probability” has in many languages other than English.

definition.value: attitude to turn away from risk (3.1.1)
element which alone or in combination has the potential to give rise to risk (3.1.1)
internal environment in which the organization (3.3.7) seeks to achieve its objectives (3.1.2)
external environment in which the organization (3.3.7) seeks to achieve its objectives (3.1.2)

scopeNote.value:
External context can include:
— the cultural, social, political, legal, regulatory, financial, technological, economic, natural and competitive environment, whether international, national, regional or local;
— key drivers and trends having impact on the objectives of the organization; and
— relationships with, and perceptions and values of, external interested parties (3.3.2).

note.value: modified — “risk” has replaced “a risk” in the definition

definition.value: terms of reference against which the significance of risk (3.1.1) is evaluated

scopeNote.value: Risk criteria are based on organizational objectives (3.1.2), and external (3.3.4) and internal context (3.3.5).
Risk criteria can be derived from standards, laws, policies and other requirements.

definition.value: person or organization (3.3.7) that can affect, be affected by, or perceives itself to be affected by a decision or activity
result to be achieved

scopeNote.value: An objective can be strategic, tactical or operational.

An objective can be expressed in other ways, e.g. as an intended outcome, a purpose, an operational criterion, as a management system objective, or by the use of other words with similar meaning (e.g. aim, goal, target).

Objectives can relate to different disciplines (such as financial, health and safety, and environmental goals) and can apply at different levels (such as strategic, organization-wide, project, product and process).

definition.value: form of risk treatment (3.3.32) involving contingent arrangements for the provision of funds to meet or modify the financial consequences (3.3.18) should they occur

note.value: modified — “risk” has replaced “a risk” in the definition

definition.value: person or entity with the accountability and authority to manage risk (3.1.1)

note.value: modified — Note 4 to entry has been deleted

definition.value: form of risk treatment (3.3.32) involving the agreed distribution of risk (3.1.1) with other parties

scopeNote.value: Legal or regulatory requirements can limit, prohibit or mandate risk sharing.
The extent to which risk is distributed can depend on the reliability and clarity of the sharing arrangements.
Risk sharing can be carried out through insurance or other forms of contract.

definition.value: state, even partial, of deficiency of information related to understanding or knowledge

scopeNote.value: Uncertainty is the root source of risk (3.1.1), namely any kind of “deficiency of information” that matters in relation to objectives (and objectives, in turn, relate to all relevant interested parties’ (3.3.2) needs and expectations).
In some cases, uncertainty can be related to the organization’s (3.3.7) context as well as to its objectives (3.1.2).

definition.value: informed decision to take a particular risk (3.1.1)

scopeNote.value: Risk acceptance can occur without risk treatment (3.3.32) or during the process of risk treatment.
Accepted risks are subject to monitoring (3.3.40) and review (3.3.41).

note.value: modified —Note 2 to entry has been deleted

definition.value: process to comprehend the nature of risk (3.1.1) and to determine the level of risk (3.3.22)

scopeNote.value: Risk analysis provides the basis for risk evaluation (3.3.25) and decisions about risk treatment (3.3.32).

definition.value: magnitude of a risk (3.1.1) or combination of risks, expressed in terms of the combination of consequences (3.3.18) and their likelihood (3.3.16)

note.value: modified — The definition has been modified

definition.value: measure of the chance of occurrence expressed as a number from 0 to 1, where 0 is impossibility and 1 is absolute certainty

scopeNote.value: See 3.3.16, Note 2 to entry.

definition.value: outcome of an event (3.3.11) affecting objectives (3.1.2)

scopeNote.value: A consequence can have positive or negative, direct or indirect, effects on objectives.
Any consequence can escalate through cascading and cumulative effects.
Consequences can be expressed qualitatively or quantitatively.

definition.value: process of finding, recognizing and describing risks (3.1.1)

scopeNote.value: Risk identification can involve historical data, theoretical analysis, informed and expert opinions, and interested party’s (3.3.2) needs.
Risk identification involves the identification of risk sources (3.3.10), events (3.3.11), their causes and their potential consequences (3.3.18).

note.value: modified — “interested party” has replaced “stakeholder”, and “residual risk” has replaced “risk after risk treatment”

definition.value: organization’s (3.3.7) or interested party’s (3.3.2) readiness to bear the residual risk (3.3.38) in order to achieve its objectives (3.1.2)

scopeNote.value: Risk tolerance can be influenced by legal or regulatory requirements.

definition.value: effect of uncertainty (3.1.3) on objectives (3.1.2)

scopeNote.value: Risk is usually expressed in terms of risk sources (3.3.10), potential events (3.3.11), their consequences (3.3.18) and their likelihood (3.3.16).
Objectives can have different aspects and categories, and can be applied at different levels.
An effect is a deviation from the expected. It can be positive, negative or both, and can address, create or result in opportunities (3.3.23) and threats (3.3.13).

note.value: modified — “interested party” has replaced “stakeholder”, and “risk” has replaced “a risk” in the definition

definition.value: interested party’s (3.3.2) view on risk (3.1.1)

scopeNote.value: Risk perception reflects the interested party’s needs, issues, knowledge, beliefs and values.

note.value: modified — “risk control” has replaced “control” in Note 1 to entry

definition.value: activity undertaken to determine the suitability, adequacy and effectiveness of the subject matter to achieve established objectives (3.1.2)

scopeNote.value: Review can be applied to a risk management framework, risk management process (3.3.1), risk (3.1.1) or risk control (3.3.33).

definition.value: source of potential harm

scopeNote.value: Hazard can be a risk source (3.3.10).

definition.value: informed decision not to be involved in, or to withdraw from, an activity in order not to be exposed to a particular risk (3.1.1)

scopeNote.value: Risk avoidance can be based on the result of risk evaluation (3.3.25) and/or legal and regulatory obligations.

definition.value: occurrence or change of a particular set of circumstances

scopeNote.value: An event can also be something that is expected which does not happen, or something that is not expected which does happen.
An event can have one or more occurrences, and can have several causes and several consequences (3.3.18).
An event can be a risk source (3.3.10).

definition.value: organization’s (3.3.7) approach to assess and eventually pursue, retain, take or turn away from risk (3.1.1)
factor that has a major influence on risk (3.1.1)
amount and type of risk (3.1.1) that an organization (3.3.7) is willing to pursue or retain
number of events (3.3.11) or outcomes per defined unit of time

scopeNote.value: Frequency can be applied to past events or to potential future events, where it can be used as a measure of likelihood (3.3.16)/probability (3.3.19).

definition.value: potential source of danger, harm, or other undesirable outcome

scopeNote.value: A threat is a negative situation in which loss is likely and over which one has relatively little control.
A threat to one party may pose an opportunity (3.3.23) to another.

definition.value: coordinated activities to direct and control an organization (3.3.7) with regard to risk (3.1.1)
scheme within the risk management framework specifying the approach, the management components and resources to be applied to the management of risk (3.1.1)

scopeNote.value: The risk management plan can be applied to a particular product, process and project, and part or whole of the organization (3.3.7).
Management components typically include procedures, practices, assignment of responsibilities, sequence and timing of activities.

definition.value: systematic application of management policies, procedures and practices to the activities of communicating, consulting, establishing the context, and identifying, analysing, evaluating, treating, monitoring (3.3.40) and reviewing risk (3.1.1)
risk (3.1.1) remaining after risk treatment (3.3.32)

scopeNote.value: Residual risk can contain unidentified risk.
Residual risk can also be known as “retained risk”.

definition.value: intrinsic properties of something resulting in susceptibility to a risk source (3.3.10) that can lead to an event (3.3.11) with a consequence (3.3.18)
adaptive capacity of an organization (3.3.7) in a complex and changing environment
overall process of risk identification (3.3.9), risk analysis (3.3.15) and risk evaluation (3.3.25)
person or group of people that has its own functions with responsibilities, authorities and relationships to achieve its objectives (3.1.2)

scopeNote.value: The concept of organization includes, but is not limited to, sole-trader, company, corporation, firm, enterprise, authority, partnership, charity or institution, or part or combination thereof, whether incorporated or not, public or private.

definition.value: combination of a number of risks (3.1.1) into one risk to develop a more complete understanding of the overall risk

systematic, independent and documented process for obtaining evidence and evaluating it objectively in order to determine the extent to which the risk management framework, or any selected part of it, is adequate and effective
